Baghdad-Iraq.name: Baghdad
Baghdad-Iraq.evidence_basis: Founded 762 by Caliph al-Mansur; Round City plus Karkh, Harbiyya and East Bank Rusafa/Shammasiyya suburbs (~7,000 ha discontinuous urban footprint at 75-100/ha; Lassner 1970, Kennedy 2004, al-Ya'qubi), peaking around 900 after the return from Samarra before 10th-c. civil wars and Buyid contraction.

Rayy-Iran.name: Rayy
Rayy-Iran.evidence_basis: Premier Iranian plateau metropolis (~1,500+ ha walled shahristan and sprawling rabad; Rante 2015, al-Muqaddasi, Ibn Hawqal), enlarged by Caliph al-Mahdi and peaking as northern Buyid capital in the late 10th c.

Samarra-Iraq.name: Samarra
Samarra-Iraq.evidence_basis: Founded 836 by al-Mu'tasim as Abbasid imperial cantonment spanning ~15,000 ha of low-density palaces and military avenues along the Tigris (Northedge 2005, al-Ya'qubi), collapsing rapidly after the caliphate returned to Baghdad in 892.

Fustat-Egypt.name: Fustat
Fustat-Egypt.evidence_basis: Founded 641 by Amr ibn al-As; grew across ~300+ ha of dense multi-storey housing plus al-Askar (750) and Tulunid al-Qata'i (870) (Kubiak 1987, Scanlon, al-Muqaddasi), remaining Egypt's commercial core alongside royal Al-Qahira after 969.

Basra-Iraq.name: Basra
Basra-Iraq.evidence_basis: Founded 638 as Rashidun garrison misr and Gulf maritime entrepot (diwan troop registers of 60k-80k fighters plus dependents; al-Baladhuri, Ashtor 1976, Kennedy 2004); devastated by the Zanj sack of 871 and Qarmatian sack of 923.

Nishapur-Iran.name: Nishapur
Nishapur-Iran.evidence_basis: Expanded from ~18 ha Sasanian core to ~1,680 ha qanat-fed Tahirid and Samanid metropolis with major cotton and ceramic industries (Bulliet 1976 topographic-demographic estimate 110k-220k; Wilkinson 1986, al-Muqaddasi).

Al-Mada'in-Iraq.name: Al-Mada'in
Al-Mada'in-Iraq.evidence_basis: Former Sasanian twin-bank imperial capital; archaeological survey (Adams 1965, Morony 1984) and Arabic chronicles document rapid depopulation after 637 conquest and dismantling for Baghdad's construction after 762.

Alexandria-Egypt.name: Alexandria
Alexandria-Egypt.evidence_basis: Contracted from Late Antique imperial scale as administration shifted inland to Fustat and walls were shortened under Ibn Tulun, stabilizing as Mediterranean naval ribat and trade port (Kubiak, Haas, Ibn Hawqal).

Kufa-Iraq.name: Kufa
Kufa-Iraq.evidence_basis: Founded 638 as Rashidun misr and capital under Caliph Ali; tribal khitat layout and diwan registers (Djait 1986, Adams 1981), declining steadily after Baghdad's foundation and Qarmatian raids in 906 and 927.

Isfahan-Iran.name: Isfahan
Isfahan-Iran.evidence_basis: Twin urban centers of Jayy and Yahudiyya in the Zayandeh Rud oasis merging into a vast Buyid commercial, silk, and cotton metropolis praised by al-Istakhri, Ibn Hawqal, and al-Muqaddasi.

Damascus-Syria.name: Damascus
Damascus-Syria.evidence_basis: 128 ha walled Roman-Umayyad core plus flourishing Ghouta/Barada suburbs (Burns 2005, al-Muqaddasi); surged as Umayyad imperial capital (661-750), then contracted under Abbasid rule after 750.

Kairouan-Tunisia.name: Kairouan
Kairouan-Tunisia.evidence_basis: Founded 670 by Uqba ibn Nafi as misr and capital of Ifriqiya; grew across extensive medina, Raqqada and Fatimid/Zirid Sabra al-Mansuriyya suburbs fed by Aghlabid basins (Fenwick 2020, Talbi 1966, Ibn Hawqal, al-Muqaddasi).

Shiraz-Iran.name: Shiraz
Shiraz-Iran.evidence_basis: Founded 693 as Umayyad military camp superseding Istakhr; rapidly grew into the capital of Fars and imperial seat of Buyid Adud al-Dawla with new satellite town Kard-Fana-Khusraw (Limbert 2004, al-Muqaddasi, Ibn Hawqal).

Balkh-Afghanistan.name: Balkh
Balkh-Afghanistan.evidence_basis: 'Mother of Cities' of eastern Khorasan; ~400 ha inner walled core plus sprawling Balkhab oasis rabad rebuilt after 725 and flourishing under Barmakid and Samanid rule (Azad 2013, al-Ya'qubi, Ibn Hawqal).

Herat-Afghanistan.name: Herat
Herat-Afghanistan.evidence_basis: One of the four great capitals of Khorasan anchored on the irrigated Harirud valley; ~200 ha walled shahristan surrounded by dense commercial suburbs (al-Istakhri, Ibn Hawqal, al-Muqaddasi).

Mosul-Iraq.name: Mosul
Mosul-Iraq.evidence_basis: Umayyad and Abbasid Upper Tigris metropolis and grain/textile entrepot (~300+ ha walled area plus extramural quarters), peaking under the Hamdanid emirs in the mid-10th c. (Robinson 2000, Ibn Hawqal, al-Muqaddasi).

Fez-Morocco.name: Fez
Fez-Morocco.evidence_basis: Founded 789 by Idris I and expanded 808-809 by Idris II into twin walled quarters (al-Qarawiyyin and al-Andalus) absorbing Qayrawani and Cordoban refugees into the western Maghreb's largest metropolis (Le Tourneau, Fenwick 2020, Ibn Hawqal).

Raqqa-Syria.name: Raqqa
Raqqa-Syria.evidence_basis: Twin Euphrates city enlarged by al-Mansur's horseshoe-walled garrison of al-Rafiqa (772) and Harun al-Rashid's imperial capital complex (796-809; >300 ha urban/industrial ceramic and glass quarters; Heidemann 2003, Ibn Hawqal).

Hamadan-Iran.name: Hamadan
Hamadan-Iran.evidence_basis: Ancient concentric-walled Jibal metropolis and major staging city on the Baghdad-Khorasan highway praised by Ibn Hawqal and al-Muqaddasi for its extensive bazaars and saffron/textile trade.

Zaranj-Afghanistan.name: Zaranj
Zaranj-Afghanistan.evidence_basis: Capital of Sistan and the Saffarid Empire (861-900); double-walled Helmand delta metropolis powered by canal irrigation and vertical-axis windmills (Bosworth 1968, Tate 1910, Ibn Hawqal).

Ghazni-Afghanistan.name: Ghazni
Ghazni-Afghanistan.evidence_basis: Highland Indo-Iranian caravan entrepot surging dramatically in the late 10th c. as imperial capital under Sabuktigin (977) and Mahmud of Ghazni (998) (Bosworth 1963, al-Istakhri, al-Muqaddasi).

Jurjan-Iran.name: Jurjan
Jurjan-Iran.evidence_basis: Excavated ~1,200 ha walled twin-bank silk emporium and Ziyarid capital linking the Iranian plateau with the Caspian and Volga steppe trade (Kiani 1984, Ibn Hawqal, al-Muqaddasi).

Barda-Azerbaijan.name: Barda
Barda-Azerbaijan.evidence_basis: Grand early Islamic capital of Arran and premier silk-trade emporium of the eastern Caucasus (al-Istakhri, Ibn Hawqal, Wordsworth 2018); permanently crippled by the devastating 943 Rus' sack and ensuing plague.

Aleppo-Syria.name: Aleppo
Aleppo-Syria.evidence_basis: Northern Syrian caravan metropolis eclipsing Qinnasrin (Sauvaget 1941, Ibn Hawqal); peaked under Hamdanid Emir Sayf al-Dawla (944-967) before suffering Nikephoros Phokas's 962 sack and the 963-964 famine.

Ani-Turkey.name: Ani
Ani-Turkey.evidence_basis: Kamsarakan hilltop fortress transformed into the booming Bagratid royal capital of Armenia in 961; Smbat II's double walls (977-989) enclosed ~80-100 ha of dense urban quarters and markets (Garsoian, Sinclair, Matthew of Edessa).

Antioch-Turkey.name: Antioch
Antioch-Turkey.evidence_basis: Contracted from Late Antique mega-walls to a resilient Abbasid thughur and Orontes commercial city (Kennedy 1992, Ibn Hawqal); dipped after Byzantine siege and reconquest in 969 before rebounding as Byzantine ducate capital.

Dvin-Armenia.name: Dvin
Dvin-Armenia.evidence_basis: Seat of the Arab ostikanate of Arminiya (~100 ha excavated citadel and dense craft quarters famous for qirmiz crimson dye; Kalantarian 1996, Ibn Hawqal); catastrophically devastated by the 893 earthquake before partial recovery.

Al-Qahira-Egypt.name: Al-Qahira
Al-Qahira-Egypt.evidence_basis: Founded 969 by Fatimid general Jawhar al-Siqilli 5.5 km NE of Fustat as a ~136 ha walled royal/military enclosure housing the caliphal court, regiments, and al-Azhar (Raymond 2000, Halm 2003), creating a ~230k twin metropolis with Fustat by 1000.

Sohar-Oman.name: Sohar
Sohar-Oman.evidence_basis: Premier 9th-10th c. Omani seaport ('emporium of the whole world', al-Istakhri, al-Muqaddasi) backed by copper smelting and the 70-km 10th-c. Falaj al-Mu'tarid irrigation hinterland (Kervran 2004, Costa & Wilkinson 1987, Biezeveld & During 2025).

Ahvaz-Iran.name: Ahvaz
Ahvaz-Iran.evidence_basis: Capital of Khuzestan and premier Abbasid sugarcane-refining and silk-trade emporium on the Karun; briefly set back by Zanj attacks in the 870s before Buyid resurgence (Ibn Hawqal, al-Muqaddasi).

Wasit-Iraq.name: Wasit
Wasit-Iraq.evidence_basis: Founded 702 by Umayyad governor al-Hajjaj ibn Yusuf as walled twin-bank administrative and Syrian garrison capital on the Tigris (~350-400 ha archaeological footprint; Safar 1945, Adams 1981, al-Muqaddasi).

Ardabil-Iran.name: Ardabil
Ardabil-Iran.evidence_basis: Primary early Islamic administrative capital and garrison metropolis of Azerbaijan; peaked under the Sajid and Sallarid dynasties (al-Istakhri, Ibn Hawqal, al-Muqaddasi).

Tinnis-Egypt.name: Tinnis
Tinnis-Egypt.evidence_basis: Hyper-dense ~100 ha island city in Lake Manzala and premier early Islamic fine-linen tiraz manufacturing emporium (Gascoigne 2007, Frantz-Murphy 1981, al-Muqaddasi, Nasir-i Khusraw).

Siraf-Iran.name: Siraf
Siraf-Iran.evidence_basis: Excavated ~250 ha multi-storey stone merchant port on the Persian Gulf handling Abbasid-Indian Ocean trade (Whitehouse 1970-2009, al-Istakhri); precipitously declined following the catastrophic 977 earthquake.

Tunis-Tunisia.name: Tunis
Tunis-Tunisia.evidence_basis: Refounded with a Coptic-built naval arsenal and canal in 698-700 to replace Carthage; expanded rapidly under Aghlabid, Fatimid and Zirid rule as Ifriqiya's premier Mediterranean port (Sebag 1998, Fenwick 2020, al-Ya'qubi).

Amol-Iran.name: Amol
Amol-Iran.evidence_basis: Largest city and capital of Tabaristan on the fertile Caspian littoral, described by Ibn Hawqal and al-Muqaddasi as surpassing Qazvin in population with flourishing silk and rice-plain trade.

Medina-Saudi Arabia.name: Medina
Medina-Saudi Arabia.evidence_basis: Rashidun imperial capital (632-656) and fertile date-palm oasis sustained by Egyptian Red Sea grain imports, religious endowments, and jurisprudential scholarship (Lecker, Kennedy 2004, al-Muqaddasi).

Tus-Iran.name: Tus
Tus-Iran.evidence_basis: Major Khorasan oasis agglomeration comprising Tabaran, Nuqan, and the rising Sanabad/Mashhad pilgrimage shrine after Imam Rida's burial in 818 (al-Muqaddasi, Ibn Hawqal).

Bust-Afghanistan.name: Bust
Bust-Afghanistan.evidence_basis: Second city of Sistan (~100+ ha walled Helmand-Arghandab confluence core plus emerging Ghaznavid Lashkari Bazar palace-cantonment by 990-1000; Schlumberger 1978, al-Istakhri, al-Muqaddasi).

Tarsus-Turkey.name: Tarsus
Tarsus-Turkey.evidence_basis: Rebuilt and heavily garrisoned by Harun al-Rashid (787) as capital of the Cilician Abbasid thughur (~80 ha fortified core plus volunteer ribats; Bosworth 1992, Ibn Hawqal); depopulated and resettled after the 965 Byzantine reconquest.

Sanaa-Yemen.name: Sanaa
Sanaa-Yemen.evidence_basis: Premier highland capital of Islamic Yemen with extensive monsoon-fed hinterland, textile weaving, and Yu'firid royal patronage (al-Hamdani, Serjeant & Lewcock 1983, al-Muqaddasi).

Istakhr-Iran.name: Istakhr
Istakhr-Iran.evidence_basis: Former Sasanian royal capital of Fars (~60 ha walled core plus suburbs; Whitcomb 1979 excavations, al-Istakhri), steadily eclipsed after Shiraz's 693 foundation.

Amid-Turkey.name: Amid
Amid-Turkey.evidence_basis: Massively fortified ~145 ha basalt-walled capital of Diyar Bakr on the Upper Tigris (Gabriel 1940, Ibn Hawqal, al-Muqaddasi), expanding into a wealthy Marwanid commercial center by 1000.

Qom-Iran.name: Qom
Qom-Iran.evidence_basis: Consolidated from seven villages by Ash'ari Arab migrants after 713 into a prosperous walled Shi'i center with detailed tax/qanat records in Hasan al-Qummi's Tarikh-i Qumm (988).

Sirjan-Iran.name: Sirjan
Sirjan-Iran.evidence_basis: Principal early Islamic capital of Kerman province (~200+ ha archaeological site surveyed by Williamson; al-Istakhri, al-Muqaddasi), beginning to yield political primacy to Bardasir/Kerman after 960.

Harran-Turkey.name: Harran
Harran-Turkey.evidence_basis: Walled ~130 ha Diyar Mudar commercial and Sabian scholarly hub; surged as last Umayyad imperial capital under Marwan II (744-750) before settling into a provincial center (Lloyd & Brice 1951, Ibn Hawqal).

Mecca-Saudi Arabia.name: Mecca
Mecca-Saudi Arabia.evidence_basis: Islam's premier sanctuary city supported by Abbasid Zubaida aqueducts and Egyptian/Yemeni grain shipments; severe demographic shock following the 930 Qarmatian sack before gradual recovery (al-Azraqi, al-Muqaddasi).

Al-Hasa-Saudi Arabia.name: Al-Hasa
Al-Hasa-Saudi Arabia.evidence_basis: Spring-fed eastern Arabian date-palm oasis expanding sharply after 899 as the heavily fortified capital of the Qarmatian state of Bahrayn (Ibn Hawqal, Nasir-i Khusraw, Madelung).

Tahert-Algeria.name: Tahert
Tahert-Algeria.evidence_basis: Founded c. 761 by Abd al-Rahman ibn Rustam as capital of the Ibadi Rustamid Imamate and major trans-Saharan entrepot (Savage 1997, Fenwick 2020); sharply reduced after its 909 destruction by the Fatimids.

Trebizond-Turkey.name: Trebizond
Trebizond-Turkey.evidence_basis: Capital of the Byzantine Theme of Chaldia and premier Black Sea customs emporium channeling Caliphate-Byzantine silk and brocade trade (Bryer & Winfield 1985, Ibn Hawqal, al-Mas'udi).

Al-Mahdiyya-Tunisia.name: Al-Mahdiyya
Al-Mahdiyya-Tunisia.evidence_basis: Founded 916 by Fatimid Caliph al-Mahdi on a heavily fortified peninsula with rock-cut naval harbor and Zawila commercial suburb (Halm 1996, Fenwick 2020, Ibn Hawqal); slightly reduced after the 973 court move to Cairo.

Carthage-Tunisia.name: Carthage
Carthage-Tunisia.evidence_basis: Byzantine Exarchate capital systematically dismantled by Hassan ibn al-Nu'man in 698; archaeological stratigraphy confirms abrupt collapse into a minor coastal hamlet superseded by Tunis (Fenwick 2020, Leone 2007).

Al-Anbar-Iraq.name: Al-Anbar
Al-Anbar-Iraq.evidence_basis: Euphrates canal intake town and first Abbasid capital (750-762) under al-Saffah before Baghdad's rise; heavily damaged in the 927 Qarmatian raid (al-Ya'qubi, Adams 1965).

Nicaea-Turkey.name: Nicaea
Nicaea-Turkey.evidence_basis: Resilient Opsikion Theme capital protected by 4.9 km double Roman walls (~140 ha); maintained continuous urban life through 7th-8th c. crises and expanded under Macedonian rule (Foss 1996, Haldon).

Ramla-Israel.name: Ramla
Ramla-Israel.evidence_basis: Founded c. 715 by Sulayman ibn Abd al-Malik as capital of Jund Filastin; ~160-200 ha excavated urban/industrial spread with White Mosque and olive-oil/ceramic workshops (Nol 2025, Avni 2014, al-Muqaddasi).

Qazvin-Iran.name: Qazvin
Qazvin-Iran.evidence_basis: Fortified Abbasid frontier garrison town (thughr) facing Daylam, enlarged with the City of Musa under Harun al-Rashid and wealthy 10th-c. textile hub (al-Ya'qubi, al-Muqaddasi).

Tbilisi-Georgia.name: Tbilisi
Tbilisi-Georgia.evidence_basis: Fortified Kura-gorge capital of the Arab Emirate of Tbilisi (est. 736) with thermal baths and multi-ethnic trade; temporarily burned by Abbasid general Bugha al-Kabir in 853 before strong Jafarid recovery (Minorsky, Ibn Hawqal).

Ganja-Azerbaijan.name: Ganja
Ganja-Azerbaijan.evidence_basis: Founded 859 by Abbasid governor Muhammad ibn Khalid; surged in the late 10th c. as capital of the Shaddadid dynasty (from 971) absorbing regional trade after Barda's decline (Minorsky 1953, Ibn Hawqal).

Mayyafariqin-Turkey.name: Mayyafariqin
Mayyafariqin-Turkey.evidence_basis: Fortified Upper Tigris piedmont city rising steeply in the 10th c. as a Hamdanid stronghold and primary capital of the Kurdish Marwanid dynasty (Ibn Hawqal, Hillenbrand 1990).

Jerusalem-Palestine.name: Jerusalem
Jerusalem-Palestine.evidence_basis: ~105 ha walled holy city sustained by Umayyad Haram al-Sharif patronage, multi-confessional pilgrimage, and ecclesiastical institutions (Avni 2014, Gil 1992, al-Muqaddasi).

Shushtar-Iran.name: Shushtar
Shushtar-Iran.evidence_basis: Hydraulic weir-irrigated Khuzestan city famed for royal dibaj brocade production and dense riverine urban quarters (al-Istakhri, al-Muqaddasi).

Tripoli-Libya.name: Tripoli
Tripoli-Libya.evidence_basis: Walled Tripolitanian maritime port and northern terminus of the Fezzan-Kanem trans-Saharan caravan corridor praised by al-Ya'qubi and Ibn Hawqal (Fenwick 2020).

Tabriz-Iran.name: Tabriz
Tabriz-Iran.evidence_basis: Strategic Azerbaijan crossroad city rebuilt after the 858 earthquake and rising under the Rawwadid emirs in the late 10th c. (Ibn Hawqal, al-Muqaddasi).

Zabid-Yemen.name: Zabid
Zabid-Yemen.evidence_basis: Founded 820 by Muhammad ibn Ziyad as walled circular capital of the Ziyadid dynasty on the irrigated Tihama plain; major indigo, textile, and scholarly center (Keall 1983, al-Muqaddasi).

Amorium-Turkey.name: Amorium
Amorium-Turkey.evidence_basis: Excavated ~75 ha walled military capital of the Anatolic Theme; catastrophically sacked by Caliph al-Mu'tasim in 838 before rebuilding on a reduced citadel-centered footprint (Lightfoot 2007, Ivison).

Homs-Syria.name: Homs
Homs-Syria.evidence_basis: Capital of Umayyad Jund Hims with heavy Yemeni Arab settlement and fertile Orontes plain (al-Ya'qubi, al-Muqaddasi); declined gradually following 9th-c. revolts and Byzantine frontier raids.

Tyre-Lebanon.name: Tyre
Tyre-Lebanon.evidence_basis: Heavily fortified island naval arsenal, glassmaking, sugar-refining, and textile port praised by al-Ya'qubi and al-Muqaddasi as the richest maritime city of the Levantine coast.

Nisibis-Turkey.name: Nisibis
Nisibis-Turkey.evidence_basis: Walled Jazira oasis and Diyar Rabi'a administrative center noted by Ibn Hawqal and al-Muqaddasi for extensive orchards, grain storage, and cross-border trade with Mosul and Armenia.

Malatya-Turkey.name: Malatya
Malatya-Turkey.evidence_basis: Principal thughur al-Jazira frontier city refortified by al-Mansur (757); Muslim garrison expelled after John Kourkouas's 934 Byzantine conquest and replaced by Syriac/Armenian settlers (Honigmann, Ibn Hawqal).

Ephesus-Turkey.name: Ephesus
Ephesus-Turkey.evidence_basis: Thrakesion Theme metropolis contracting from silted lower city onto fortified Ayasoluk hill around St. John's basilica; revived by major annual fairs and 9th-10th c. agrarian expansion (Foss 1979, Vroom 2025, Preiser-Kapeller 2024).

Damietta-Egypt.name: Damietta
Damietta-Egypt.evidence_basis: Eastern Nile branch maritime port and tiraz textile center; temporarily depopulated by the 853 Byzantine naval raid, then fortified and booming under Tulunid and Fatimid commerce (Frantz-Murphy 1981, al-Muqaddasi).

Sousse-Tunisia.name: Sousse
Sousse-Tunisia.evidence_basis: Walled ~32 ha Aghlabid maritime port, ribat fortress, and textile-weaving city serving as main naval embarkation base for the conquest of Sicily (827) (Lezine, Fenwick 2020, Ibn Hawqal).

Maragha-Iran.name: Maragha
Maragha-Iran.evidence_basis: Walled fertile Azerbaijan provincial capital and Abbasid-Sajid military headquarters south of Mount Sahand (Ibn Hawqal, al-Muqaddasi).

Attaleia-Turkey.name: Attaleia
Attaleia-Turkey.evidence_basis: Heavily walled naval headquarters of the Cibyrrhaeot Theme and key Levantine-Byzantine commercial entrepot noted by Ibn Hawqal and Foss (1996).

Edessa-Turkey.name: Edessa
Edessa-Turkey.evidence_basis: Walled ~140 ha Syriac Christian and Islamic Jazira urban center (Segal 1970, Ibn Hawqal); moderately reduced by the 944 Byzantine siege and 963-964 northern Syrian famine.

Aden-Yemen.name: Aden
Aden-Yemen.evidence_basis: Strategic crater-harbor entrepot linking Red Sea, East Africa, and Indian Ocean shipping lanes; noted by al-Muqaddasi and Ibn Hawqal as a thriving customs port.

Asyut-Egypt.name: Asyut
Asyut-Egypt.evidence_basis: Principal Upper Egyptian provincial market, Darb al-Arba'in caravan terminus, and wool/linen manufacturing city described by al-Ya'qubi and al-Muqaddasi.

Shamakhi-Azerbaijan.name: Shamakhi
Shamakhi-Azerbaijan.evidence_basis: Walled Shirvan silk- and wine-producing hub elevated to capital of the Shirvanshahs as Yazidiyya in 918 (Minorsky 1958, al-Istakhri).

Tlemcen-Algeria.name: Tlemcen
Tlemcen-Algeria.evidence_basis: Walled western Algerian administrative hub expanding under the Banu Ifran (Abu Qurra) and Idrisids as a crossroads between Fez, Tahert, and the Mediterranean ports (Fenwick 2020, Ibn Hawqal).

Kabul-Afghanistan.name: Kabul
Kabul-Afghanistan.evidence_basis: Fortified Kabul Shahi citadel and bilingual Hindu-Muslim frontier indigo/caravan entrepot linking Khorasan to Gandhara (al-Istakhri, Ibn Hawqal, Hudud al-Alam).

Tripoli-Lebanon.name: Tripoli
Tripoli-Lebanon.evidence_basis: Fortified peninsula harbor resettled under Mu'awiya and developed into a major Tulunid and Fatimid naval base and papermaking/silk port (al-Ya'qubi, al-Muqaddasi).

Damghan-Iran.name: Damghan
Damghan-Iran.evidence_basis: Provincial capital of Qumis on the Great Khorasan Silk Road with 8th-c. Tarikhaneh mosque and thriving textile workshops (al-Muqaddasi, Ibn Hawqal).

Al-Faiyum-Egypt.name: Al-Faiyum
Al-Faiyum-Egypt.evidence_basis: Capital of the irrigated Fayyum oasis basin with dense canal network, sugarcane and flax production documented in early Islamic papyri (Sijpesteijn 2013, al-Muqaddasi).

Acre-Israel.name: Acre
Acre-Israel.evidence_basis: Umayyad shipyard and Levantine port significantly expanded after Ahmad ibn Tulun constructed its fortified sea-harbor breakwater c. 878 (al-Muqaddasi, Avni 2014).

Sabta-Morocco.name: Sabta
Sabta-Morocco.evidence_basis: Heavily fortified Strait of Gibraltar naval base annexed and expanded by Cordoban Caliph Abd al-Rahman III in 931 as principal maritime bridgehead between al-Andalus and the Maghreb (Ibn Hawqal, Fenwick 2020).

Aswan-Egypt.name: Aswan
Aswan-Egypt.evidence_basis: Southern Nubian frontier ribat, baqt treaty trade station, and Eastern Desert Wadi al-Allaqi gold-rush hub peaking in the 9th-10th c. (al-Ya'qubi, Ibn Hawqal, Garcin 1976).

Nahrawan-Iraq.name: Nahrawan
Nahrawan-Iraq.evidence_basis: Major Diyala-plain market and bridge town on the Great Khorasan Road east of Baghdad (~150 ha Abbasid settlement survey; Adams 1965 Land Behind Baghdad), declining after the 937 breach of the Nahrawan canal.

Yazd-Iran.name: Yazd
Yazd-Iran.evidence_basis: Qanat-irrigated central desert oasis hub on the Fars-Khorasan caravan axis renowned for cotton and silk textiles (al-Istakhri, al-Muqaddasi).

Caesarea-Turkey.name: Caesarea
Caesarea-Turkey.evidence_basis: Cappadocian metropolitan and major Byzantine military staging base recovering strongly in the 9th-10th c. as the eastern frontier pushed past the Taurus (Cooper & Decker 2012, Preiser-Kapeller 2024).

Aghmat-Morocco.name: Aghmat
Aghmat-Morocco.evidence_basis: High Atlas piedmont oasis and principal commercial capital of southern Morocco before Marrakech (c. 1070), with excavated early Islamic hammam and mosque complex (Messier & Fili, al-Ya'qubi, Ibn Hawqal).

Ascalon-Israel.name: Ascalon
Ascalon-Israel.evidence_basis: Walled ~60 ha fortified coastal ribat and Mediterranean export hub flourishing under Abbasid, Ikhshidid and early Fatimid rule (al-Muqaddasi, Avni 2014).

Tiberias-Israel.name: Tiberias
Tiberias-Israel.evidence_basis: ~65 ha lakeside capital of Jund al-Urdunn with excavated Umayyad-Abbasid congregational mosque, markets and thermal baths; brief dip after the 749 Galilee earthquake (Walmsley 2007, Avni 2014, al-Muqaddasi).

Maymana-Afghanistan.name: Maymana
Maymana-Afghanistan.evidence_basis: Capital of Guzgan under the Farighunid dynasty (9th-10th c.), flourishing as a wool-carpet and horse-trading hub between Balkh and Herat (Hudud al-Alam, al-Muqaddasi).

Kars-Turkey.name: Kars
Kars-Turkey.evidence_basis: Fortified Armenian plateau town elevated to Bagratid royal capital (929-961) under King Abas I before serving as seat of the Kingdom of Kars (Garsoian, Ibn Hawqal).

Smyrna-Turkey.name: Smyrna
Smyrna-Turkey.evidence_basis: Aegean harbor and naval base of the Samos/Thrakesion Themes; contracted during 7th-8th c. Arab maritime raids before rebounding with 9th-10th c. Aegean commercial revival (Ahrweiler, Foss).

Akhmim-Egypt.name: Akhmim
Akhmim-Egypt.evidence_basis: Major Upper Egyptian Coptic-Islamic urban hub famous for fine linen weaving and monumental temples noted by Ibn Hawqal and al-Muqaddasi.

Kutaisi-Georgia.name: Kutaisi
Kutaisi-Georgia.evidence_basis: Rioni River stronghold expanding rapidly after becoming capital of the Kingdom of Abkhazia (778) and unified Georgia under Bagrat III around 1000 (Rayfield 2012).

Al-Ashmunayn-Egypt.name: Al-Ashmunayn
Al-Ashmunayn-Egypt.evidence_basis: Major Middle Egyptian kura administrative center and Coptic episcopal/textile city attested in Arabic-Coptic tax papyri and al-Ya'qubi (Sijpesteijn 2013).

Sebasteia-Turkey.name: Sebasteia
Sebasteia-Turkey.evidence_basis: Eastern Anatolian crossroad elevated to capital of the Theme of Sebasteia in 911 and bolstered by substantial 10th-c. Armenian settlement (Preiser-Kapeller 2024, Matthew of Edessa).

Constantia-Cyprus.name: Constantia
Constantia-Cyprus.evidence_basis: Late Antique metropolitan capital of Cyprus devastated by Mu'awiya's naval raids of 649 and 653, shrinking to a fortified residual nucleus as inhabitants relocated toward Nicosia and Famagusta (Metcalf 2009, Zavagno 2017).

Nicosia-Cyprus.name: Nicosia
Nicosia-Cyprus.evidence_basis: Sheltered inland Mesaoria town rising steadily as refugees abandoned exposed coastal cities during the 688-965 Arab-Byzantine condominium, becoming Byzantine Theme capital after 965 (Metcalf 2009, Zavagno 2017).

Qinnasrin-Syria.name: Qinnasrin
Qinnasrin-Syria.evidence_basis: Umayyad capital of Jund Qinnasrin; archaeological survey (Whitcomb 2000) and Ibn Hawqal confirm steady urban contraction in the 9th-10th c. as population shifted 27 km north to Aleppo.

Qus-Egypt.name: Qus
Qus-Egypt.evidence_basis: Rising Upper Egyptian Nile-bend town overtaking Qift in the 10th c. as primary commercial gateway to Eastern Desert mines and Red Sea routes (Garcin 1976, al-Ya'qubi).

Barqa-Libya.name: Barqa
Barqa-Libya.evidence_basis: Fortified early Islamic provincial capital of Cyrenaica on the fertile Jabal Akhdar plain, major wool/leather market and Fatimid staging point for Egypt (al-Ya'qubi, Ibn Hawqal, al-Muqaddasi).

Tangier-Morocco.name: Tangier
Tangier-Morocco.evidence_basis: Strategic Strait of Gibraltar port and early Umayyad launchpad for the 711 Iberian crossing, fortified under Idrisid and Cordoban Umayyad maritime networks (al-Ya'qubi, Ibn Hawqal).

Constantine-Algeria.name: Constantine
Constantine-Algeria.evidence_basis: Naturally fortified Rhumel-gorge city serving as western Ifriqiya's grain, wool, and Fatimid-Kutama administrative center (Ibn Hawqal, al-Muqaddasi).

Kunduz-Afghanistan.name: Kunduz
Kunduz-Afghanistan.evidence_basis: Principal irrigated valley city and administrative seat of eastern Tokharistan noted by al-Istakhri and the Hudud al-Alam.

Kandahar-Afghanistan.name: Kandahar
Kandahar-Afghanistan.evidence_basis: Arachosia oasis stronghold and Indian transit market attested archaeologically at Old Kandahar and in al-Istakhri's account of al-Rukhkhaj (Helms 1997).

Iconium-Turkey.name: Iconium
Iconium-Turkey.evidence_basis: Fortified central Anatolian plateau kastro and agrarian market on the military road to Cilicia, expanding with 9th-10th c. Byzantine stabilization (Belke, Haldon).

Tikrit-Iraq.name: Tikrit
Tikrit-Iraq.evidence_basis: Fortified Tigris river crossing, Syriac Orthodox maphrianate seat and wool/raft trade center boosted during Samarra's nearby caliphal floruit (Ibn Hawqal, Robinson 2000).

Msila-Algeria.name: Msila
Msila-Algeria.evidence_basis: Founded 927 by Fatimid heir al-Qa'im as a walled Hodna-plain garrison and administrative capital commanding the central Maghreb steppes (Ibn Hawqal, Fenwick 2020).

Hama-Syria.name: Hama
Hama-Syria.evidence_basis: Walled Orontes river town with noria irrigation and regional textile markets expanding steadily during the Abbasid and Hamdanid centuries (Ibn Hawqal, al-Muqaddasi).

Gaza-Palestine.name: Gaza
Gaza-Palestine.evidence_basis: Southern Palestinian caravan terminus and coastal market linking Bilad al-Sham, Hijaz, and Egypt; continuous urban occupation documented by al-Muqaddasi and Avni (2014).

Marash-Turkey.name: Marash
Marash-Turkey.evidence_basis: Fortified Syrian-Anatolian thughur garrison commanding the Taurus passes, repeatedly rebuilt under Abbasids and recaptured by Byzantium in 952 (al-Baladhuri, Ibn Hawqal).

Nakhchivan-Azerbaijan.name: Nakhchivan
Nakhchivan-Azerbaijan.evidence_basis: Strategic Aras valley river-crossing fortress and Arab-Sajid garrison/commercial town linking Dvin with Azerbaijan (al-Istakhri, Ibn Hawqal).

Ancyra-Turkey.name: Ancyra
Ancyra-Turkey.evidence_basis: Shrank into a heavily fortified hilltop kastro during 7th-8th c. Arab raids and the 838 sack, then recovered as Boukellarion Theme administrative hub in the 9th-10th c. (Foss 1977, Haldon).

Theodosiopolis-Turkey.name: Theodosiopolis
Theodosiopolis-Turkey.evidence_basis: Heavily fortified Abbasid frontier emirate of Qaliqala controlling the Armenian highlands trade route; captured and depopulated by Byzantium in 949 before recovery (Ibn Hawqal, Sinclair).

Ashir-Algeria.name: Ashir
Ashir-Algeria.evidence_basis: Founded 935-936 by Ziri ibn Manad in the Titteri mountains with Fatimid architectural aid as the fortified capital of the Sanhaja Zirids (Golvin 1966 excavations, Ibn Hawqal).

Sa'da-Yemen.name: Sa'da
Sa'da-Yemen.evidence_basis: Northern Yemeni highland ironworking and leather-tanning hub expanding rapidly after becoming seat of the Zaydi Imamate in 897 (al-Hamdani, al-Muqaddasi).

Gabes-Tunisia.name: Gabes
Gabes-Tunisia.evidence_basis: Coastal date-palm oasis and silk-producing port linking southern Ifriqiya with Tripolitania and trans-Saharan caravans (al-Ya'qubi, Ibn Hawqal).

Jeddah-Saudi Arabia.name: Jeddah
Jeddah-Saudi Arabia.evidence_basis: Designated official Red Sea port of Mecca by Caliph Uthman in 647; described by al-Muqaddasi as a fortified, wealthy grain-importing and pilgrim-disembarkation town with Persian and Egyptian merchants.

Beylagan-Azerbaijan.name: Beylagan
Beylagan-Azerbaijan.evidence_basis: Excavated ~40 ha walled city at Oren-Qala in the Mil steppe of Arran with flourishing glazed-ceramic and metalwork workshops (Akhmedov, al-Istakhri, Ibn Hawqal).

Nizwa-Oman.name: Nizwa
Nizwa-Oman.evidence_basis: Interior Jabal Akhdar oasis capital of the First Ibadi Imamate (793-893) supported by extensive aflaj irrigation and scholarly networks (Wilkinson 1977, al-Muqaddasi).

Palmyra-Syria.name: Palmyra
Palmyra-Syria.evidence_basis: Umayyad desert oasis town with excavated colonnaded suq and Kalbite stronghold (Genequand 2012); sharply reduced after Marwan II demolished its walls following the 745 revolt.

Awal-Bahrain.name: Awal
Awal-Bahrain.evidence_basis: Excavated early Islamic urban core at Bilad al-Qadim and Qal'at al-Bahrain sustained by Gulf pearl fisheries, date groves, and Qarmatian customs tolls (Insoll 2005, al-Istakhri).

Al-Qatif-Saudi Arabia.name: Al-Qatif
Al-Qatif-Saudi Arabia.evidence_basis: Fortified eastern Arabian coastal oasis, pearling harbor, and Qarmatian maritime outlet on the Persian Gulf (al-Muqaddasi, Ibn Hawqal).

Sale-Morocco.name: Sale
Sale-Morocco.evidence_basis: Atlantic Bou Regreg estuary port and fortified ribat facing the Barghawata confederation, documented by Ibn Hawqal and early Islamic excavations at Chellah.

Bamiyan-Afghanistan.name: Bamiyan
Bamiyan-Afghanistan.evidence_basis: Strategic Hindu Kush pass entrepot and principality of the Shir-i Bamiyan linking Balkh to Kabul (al-Ya'qubi, Hudud al-Alam, al-Muqaddasi).

Sinope-Turkey.name: Sinope
Sinope-Turkey.evidence_basis: Walled peninsula harbor and Paphlagonian naval/trade station linking Constantinople with Cherson and Trebizond (Bryer & Winfield 1985).

Beirut-Lebanon.name: Beirut
Beirut-Lebanon.evidence_basis: Gradually recovering from the 551 earthquake as Damascus's maritime outlet, coastal ribat and seat of jurist al-Awza'i (al-Ya'qubi, al-Muqaddasi).

Nakur-Morocco.name: Nakur
Nakur-Morocco.evidence_basis: Founded 710 as capital of the Salihid Emirate of Nekor in the Rif valley; suffered Viking raid (859) and repeated 10th-c. Fatimid sacks (al-Ya'qubi, Ibn Hawqal, Fenwick 2020).

Amman-Jordan.name: Amman
Amman-Jordan.evidence_basis: Balqa administrative capital featuring the excavated Umayyad citadel palace complex, mint, and lower-town markets (Northedge 1992, Walmsley 2007, al-Muqaddasi).

Al-Farama-Egypt.name: Al-Farama
Al-Farama-Egypt.evidence_basis: Fortified eastern Delta-Sinai coastal port and customs gateway between Egypt and Bilad al-Sham; gradually silting as maritime traffic favored Tinnis and Damietta (al-Muqaddasi, Ibn Hawqal).

Hajr al-Yamama-Saudi Arabia.name: Hajr al-Yamama
Hajr al-Yamama-Saudi Arabia.evidence_basis: Wadi Hanifa oasis capital of central Arabia (modern Riyadh site) supplying wheat to the Hijaz before declining amid late 9th-10th c. Ukhaydirid and Qarmatian turmoil (al-Hamdani, al-Ya'qubi).

Shibam-Yemen.name: Shibam
Shibam-Yemen.evidence_basis: Principal fortified urban center and frankincense/caravan market of Wadi Hadramawt attested by al-Hamdani and al-Muqaddasi.

Muscat-Oman.name: Muscat
Muscat-Oman.evidence_basis: Deep-water fresh-water provisioning anchorage for India- and China-bound dhows departing Sohar and Siraf (Ibn al-Faqih, al-Muqaddasi).

Ajdabiya-Libya.name: Ajdabiya
Ajdabiya-Libya.evidence_basis: Excavated Fatimid fortified palace-town and mosque hub on the Cyrenaica-Tripolitania caravan road with Saharan trade links via Awjila (Whitehouse 1972, al-Ya'qubi, Ibn Hawqal).

Ghadames-Libya.name: Ghadames
Ghadames-Libya.evidence_basis: Walled spring-fed Saharan oasis and Ibadi Berber caravan entrepot connecting Tripolitania and Ifriqiya with the central Sahara (al-Ya'qubi, Ibn Hawqal, Mattingly).

Paphos-Cyprus.name: Paphos
Paphos-Cyprus.evidence_basis: Western Cypriot harbor briefly occupied by an Arab garrison after 653; maintained reduced episcopal and maritime activity during the condominium before post-965 Byzantine revival (Zavagno 2017).

Ayla-Jordan.name: Ayla
Ayla-Jordan.evidence_basis: Walled early Islamic Red Sea port and pilgrim junction (~2.5 ha fortified core plus extramural mercantile quarters excavated by Whitcomb 1994; al-Muqaddasi).
